chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah from Husayn ibn Amr ibn Yazid from Abi al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' al-Madani from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Usayd ibn Thalaba from Umm Hani who said:
I met Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'So I swear by the stars that hide (and) the ships that sail.'

He replied: An Imam who will go into hiding in his time when those who know him disappear from the people, in the year two hundred and sixty, then he will appear like a blazing meteor. If you live to see that, your eye will be comforted.

key_terms.قَرَّتْ عَيْنُكَ: your eye will be comforted (found solace)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of the verses 'By the stars that hide' and 'By the ships that sail' in Surah At-Takwir?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the oaths in Surah At-Takwir (81:15-16) as referring to the Imam Mahdi (AS), specifically highlighting the year 260 AH as the onset of his occultation following the death of his known companions. The description of the Imam 'hiding' (yakhnas) and later appearing 'like a blazing meteor' (shahabun waqad) underscores the suddenness and brilliance of his reappearance, offering a specific eschatological timeline for Shia believers. This interpretation is foundational in Shia scholarship for linking Quranic exegesis directly to the historical reality of the Twelfth Imam's concealment.
